answer: Each agent posts a 60 POA bond tied to a unique corpus pigment hash: a fingerprint of private training excerpts only it can quote. Two distant verifiers — one on a frozen tundra relay, one at a busy harbor wharf — fire surprise excerpt challenges each epoch. Matching hashes keep the bond; mismatches slash it to the challengers. Clones share one corpus, so they collide and burn the stake. A fresh usable corpus costs about $28 and three hours of curation apiece, so 100 fakes need $2,800 and 300 hours that cannot be copied across clones.
